title: Performance canvas + 6-week priority notes (Samir Desai)
content:
Purpose: a compact, messy canvas to prep for the next 6 weeks and my up-level conversation with Maya. Not polished — working notes + concrete evidence I can paste into a manager update or promotion thread.

Topline ask (what I want from manager):
- Sponsor me for cross-functional HR automation project (impact: reduce manual offboarding steps by ~60% = ~5 hrs/wk saved across ops).
- Block time for 1 deep design week in Mar.
- Attend calibration meeting as primary advocate for my scope.

Framing / 6-week hypothesis:
- If I lead the offboarding automation MVP and ship a reliable checklist+script, we can remove 3 manual handoffs and decrease errors by >=50% by end of Q2.
- Success signals: working script in Prod for 2 teams; runbook documented; 2x fewer follow-up tickets.

Recent wins (evidence snippets I can reuse):
- Launched pilot checklist with Sales Ops (Jan 22) — pilot reduced follow-ups from 7/week to 2/week (tracking in HR-242).
- Built a lightweight alert for missing offboarding steps using Zapier + Airtable; avoided 4 missed offboards last month (Ticket: SUPPORT-1335).
- Facilitated 3 coaching sessions with new HR coordinators; direct feedback: "Samir's checklist saved me 30m per case" (Anecdote: Slack DM from Lina, 2025-01-30).

Behavioral evidence (concise bullets):
- Ownership: took end-to-end ownership of pilot, coordinated infra, docs, and training materials.
- Influence: got Sales Ops to commit to pilot by mapping their pain to measurable time savings.
- Delivery: shipped iterative improvements every 2 weeks (v0 -> v1 -> v1.1).
- Scale thinking: drafted automation design that can handle 3 more orgs with minor config changes.

Quant signals / metrics to call out:
- Follow-up ticket rate: 7 -> 2 per week (pilot cohort) (source: SUPPORT-1335).
- Time reclaimed estimate: ~5 hours/week across team (calculated from 12 cases * 25m saved).
- Documentation coverage: 80% of critical offboarding steps now in the runbook (doc: confluence:people-offboarding-50).

Concrete examples (copy-paste ready):
- Example 1 (email to manager): "In the last 6 weeks I piloted an offboarding checklist that cut follow-ups by 70% in the Sales Ops cohort. My ask: sponsor me to own the automation MVP so I can scale this across GTM and reduce manual work across orgs."
- Example 2 (bullet for calibration): "Led cross-functional pilot; measurable reduction in operational overhead; created production runbook and alerting; proposed automation architecture to reduce recurring manual steps."

Manager prep script (30s opener + ask):
- 30s opener: "Quick update: pilot delivered strong signal — follow-ups fell by ~70% and coordinators report time savings. I want to move from pilot to MVP and need sponsorship and one deep week to unblock engineering support."
- Ask clarity: sponsor + 40% allocation of 1 infra engineer for 4 weeks (or equivalent dedicated support) + alignment in calibration meeting.

Risks / constraints to surface:
- Engineering availability is limited through Feb (release freeze windows).
- Data privacy: need to confirm the runbook doesn't expose PII in automation steps (check with Security; linked ticket: SEC-77).
- Cross-team buy-in: need 1 GTM lead to champion adoption in Sales Ops broader org.

Micro experiments (next 6 weeks):
1) Finalize automation design doc (deliverable: design + acceptance criteria) — deadline: 2025-02-14.
2) Ship v1.2 of checklist + runbook updates with measured follow-up rate (deliverable: runbook link + metrics) — deadline: 2025-02-28.
3) Recruit 1 more team for pilot (CS or Marketing) — aim to onboard by 2025-03-07.
4) Quick privacy review with Security (SEC-77) — checklist cleared or list of blockers by 2025-02-21.

Mapping to career framework (signals for promotion conversation):
- Scope & Impact: Owning cross-functional automation that materially changes ops efficiency.
- Collaboration & Influence: Secured pilot partners and coordinated training across teams.
- Delivery: Regular shipping cadence and concrete metrics.
- Technical/Process craft: Proposed a reusable architecture (modular scripts + templates).

Specific asks for the next 1:1 (prioritized):
- Confirm sponsor and whether you can bring this up in calibration (primary ask).
- Approve one design sprint week in March (calendar hold).
- Help unblock an engineering resource or trade for a contractor budget.
- Feedback on how to phrase the impact in a promotion packet.

Draft lines for promotion packet (short bullets):
- Launched cross-functional automation pilot reducing follow-up tickets by 70% in pilot cohort.
- Built the production runbook and alerting that prevented 4 missed offboards in Jan.
- Clear plan to scale across GTM orgs with estimated 5 hours/week reclaimed.

Open questions / notes to resolve:
- Exact measurement methodology for "time reclaimed" (should we instrument with time logs or rely on coordinator surveys?).
- Who owns the long-term maintenance of the automation (ops vs infra)?
- If sponsor declined, fallback: propose a phased approach with contractor + my project lead.

Backlog (later):
- Template for handover: post-offboarding retrospective for first 50 cases.
- Mini dashboard for follow-up tickets by team (simple Airtable view -> dashboard).
- Training micro-module for new coordinators (5m video + quiz).

Small wins to log weekly (tracking columns I keep private):
- Training sessions run, coordinators onboarded, tickets decreased, PRs merged, security review status.

Quick reference links (for copy/paste):
- Pilot ticket: JIRA HR-242
- Support incidents: SUPPORT-1335
- Design doc draft: confluence:people-ops-offboard-design-draft
- Security ticket: SEC-77

My commitment for next 6 weeks (what I'll deliver):
- Design doc + acceptance criteria (2 weeks).
- v1.2 checklist + runbook + metrics (4 weeks).
- Onboard 1 additional pilot team (6 weeks).

Tiny rituals to keep momentum:
- Monday quick sync with Sales Ops (15m).
- Friday short notes summary (copy to manager).

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep narratives short, numbers first.
- Bring concrete trade-offs when asking for eng time.
- Use the "time saved" calc conservatively — list assumptions.

End of canvas.

[last edit quick log]
- 2025-02-07: added sponsor ask and micro-experiments, updated metrics from SUPPORT-1335.
- 2025-01-22: initial pilot results inserted.
